class.name: FoliageSpawner3D
class.brief_description: Scatters instances of a [Mesh] (with optional LOD levels) procedurally inside a configurable box volume.
class.description: [FoliageSpawner3D] fills a box-shaped volume with randomly placed and oriented copies of a mesh (see [member lod_levels]), similar to Unreal Engine's Procedural Foliage Spawner. It is a specialized [MultiMeshInstance3D], but its own inherited [member MultiMeshInstance3D.multimesh] is left empty and should not be edited directly: generated instances are instead stored and rendered through internal per-cell [MultiMesh]es (see [b]Cell chunking[/b] below). The volume to fill is defined by [member volume_size], centered on the node's origin. Placement is controlled by [member density] (points per square meter of the volume's footprint) and [member min_distance] (a minimum spacing enforced between instances so they don't overlap). A grayscale [member distribution_mask] can be assigned to bias or forbid placement in specific areas, and [member seed] makes generation reproducible. If [member project_on_mesh] is enabled (the default), each candidate point is projected straight down onto the surface of the [MeshInstance3D] or [Landscape3D] referenced by [member ground_mesh_path], and points whose surface is steeper than [member max_slope_degrees] are discarded; otherwise points are distributed freely throughout the volume's height. For a [MeshInstance3D], placement only looks at its [Mesh] geometry, never at a [CollisionShape3D] or other physics collider, since a collider can differ noticeably in shape from the mesh it is meant to represent; for a [Landscape3D], its height field is sampled directly (see [method TerrainData.get_height_at_position]), which is both cheaper and exact. Instances can optionally be tilted to align with the surface normal ([member align_to_normal]) and receive random rotation, extra random tilt, and random uniform scale for natural-looking variation. Nothing is generated automatically: call [method regenerate] (or press the [b]Regenerate[/b] button in the Inspector) whenever the volume, mesh, ground mesh, or any distribution setting changes. The result is saved with the scene, so no extra runtime cost is paid on load. To scatter several kinds of vegetation in the same area, add multiple [FoliageSpawner3D] nodes. [b]LOD levels:[/b] generated instances are rendered through a chain of [FoliageLODLevel]s (see [member lod_levels]), e.g. a detailed mesh up close and a cheaper one (or none at all) far away, each with its own visibility/fade distance range and optional material override - all levels share the exact same generated instance transforms, only their mesh/material/range differ. A newly created [FoliageSpawner3D] starts with three levels with reasonable default distances; add a [Mesh] to at least the first one before calling [method regenerate]. [b]Cell chunking:[/b] generated instances are stored split into a grid of cells on the local XZ plane, sized by [member cell_size]; each non-empty cell is rendered through one internal [MultiMeshInstance3D] per LOD level, the same technique [FoliagePainter3D] uses for its painted layers. A single giant [MultiMesh] would always be drawn in full once any part of it is visible, since the renderer only culls whole nodes by their bounding box; splitting it into many small, tightly-bounded cells lets the renderer's normal per-node frustum culling skip whole cells that are off-screen instead. Enable [member debug_show_cells] to draw each cell's bounds in the 3D viewport, and check [member cell_count] / [member instance_count] in the Inspector to see the result of the last [method regenerate]. [b]GPU culling:[/b] [member gpu_culling] replaces that whole scheme with per-instance culling on the GPU. Cells are not used at all: every instance is uploaded once into a single buffer, and each frame a compute pass tests each of them against the camera frustum and against its LOD level's distance band, compacting the survivors into one indirect [MultiMesh] per level (see [member MultiMesh.use_indirect]). Cell chunking can only skip whole cells, so a cell that is half on screen still draws every instance in it; the compute pass drops individual instances instead, and picks each one's LOD level by its own distance rather than the distance to the cell it happens to sit in. See [member gpu_culling] for its requirements and limitations. [b]Cell rendering:[/b] [FoliageSpawner3D] itself never has any visible geometry of its own (its inherited [MultiMesh] is always empty), so its inherited [GeometryInstance3D] properties ([member GeometryInstance3D.material_override], [member GeometryInstance3D.cast_shadow], [member GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode], [member GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_begin], etc.) would have no visible effect and are hidden in the Inspector. Use the [code]cell_*[/code] properties instead ([member cell_cast_shadow], [member cell_gi_mode], and so on, shared across every LOD level - the per-level [member FoliageLODLevel.material_override] and [member FoliageLODLevel.visibility_range_begin] and related properties live on [member lod_levels] instead): they are copied onto every cell's [MultiMeshInstance3D] and, unlike every other [FoliageSpawner3D] property, apply immediately to already-generated cells without needing to press [b]Regenerate[/b] again. [member cell_gi_mode] defaults to [constant GeometryInstance3D.GI_MODE_DISABLED]: grass and other small scattered foliage rarely benefit visually from baked or dynamic global illumination, and skipping it avoids [LightmapGI] trying to lightmap every scattered instance and avoids the per-instance cost of looking up nearby GI probes. Set [member cell_gi_mode] to [constant GeometryInstance3D.GI_MODE_DYNAMIC] for larger foliage where the difference is worth it.

method.name: has_any_mesh
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if at least one entry in [member lod_levels] has a [member FoliageLODLevel.mesh] assigned, i.e. this spawner actually generates something. [method regenerate] does nothing while this returns [code]false[/code].

method.name: regenerate
method.description: Discards the current cells and generates a new set according to the node's current settings, using [member seed] to seed the random number generator. This can be called both in the editor and at runtime; it requires the node to be inside the [SceneTree] when [member project_on_mesh] is enabled, since it needs to resolve [member ground_mesh_path] and read the referenced node's [Mesh] geometry.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], instances are tilted so their up axis follows the surface normal found by [member project_on_mesh] (blended in by [member align_to_normal_amount]). Has no effect when [member project_on_mesh] is [code]false[/code].
Blends each instance's up axis between world up ([code]0.0[/code]) and the surface normal ([code]1.0[/code]) when [member align_to_normal] is enabled.

The shadow casting mode applied to every cell. See [b]Cell rendering[/b] in the class description. An individual LOD level can still drop out of the shadow passes through [member FoliageLODLevel.cast_shadows], which is the usual way to keep shadows on nearby foliage only.

Read-only. The number of non-empty cells created by the last [method regenerate] call. See [b]Cell chunking[/b] in the class description. Always [code]0[/code] while [member gpu_culling] is enabled, which does not use cells.
The extra cull margin applied to every cell. See [b]Cell rendering[/b] in the class description.
The global illumination mode applied to every cell. See [b]Cell rendering[/b] in the class description.
Applied to every cell. See [b]Cell rendering[/b] in the class description.
Applied to every cell. See [b]Cell rendering[/b] in the class description.
The LOD bias applied to every cell. See [b]Cell rendering[/b] in the class description.
The material overlay applied to every cell. See [b]Cell rendering[/b] in the class description.

The size (in meters, on the local XZ plane) of the grid cells that generated instances are chunked into. See [b]Cell chunking[/b] in the class description. Larger values mean fewer, bigger cells (coarser culling, less overhead); smaller values mean finer-grained culling at the cost of more internal [MultiMeshInstance3D] nodes. A good starting point is a value somewhat larger than the average distance instances need to be visible from.
The transparency applied to every cell. See [b]Cell rendering[/b] in the class description.
If [code]true[/code], the editor gizmo draws the bounds of every cell created by the last [method regenerate] call, in addition to the volume box. See [b]Cell chunking[/b] in the class description.

The target number of instances per square meter of the volume's XZ footprint ([member volume_size].x × [member volume_size].z). The actual instance count is also limited by [member max_instances], [member min_distance], [member distribution_mask], and [member project_on_mesh].

An optional grayscale mask sampled across the volume's XZ footprint (black = 0.0, white = 1.0) and used as the probability that a given candidate point is kept. Set [member mask_invert] to flip which areas are favored.

If [code]true[/code], visibility is decided per instance by a compute pass on the GPU instead of per cell by the renderer. See [b]GPU culling[/b] in the class description. Toggling this keeps whatever was generated: the two paths hold the same instances in different shapes (flat for the GPU, chunked into cells for the renderer) and are converted between, so there is no need to call [method regenerate] again. This pays off when a lot of instances share the screen with a lot of instances that are off it: dense grass over a wide area, or a low [member cell_size] that would otherwise cost many draw calls. It does not pay off for a handful of instances, where the compute dispatch costs more than it saves. [b]Note:[/b] Requires the Forward+ or Mobile rendering method; the Compatibility renderer cannot draw indirect [MultiMesh]es and this falls back to cell chunking there. [b]Note:[/b] Shadows are noticeably more expensive here than with cell chunking, and can cost more than the culling saves. The compute pass culls against the camera, and every pass then draws that same set, so each shadow cascade rasterizes all camera-visible instances instead of just the cells that overlap it. Automatic mesh LOD is also lost: the renderer picks it from the distance to the nearest point of an instance's bounds, and one node covering every instance puts that distance at zero, so the highest-detail mesh is used at any range. Both are reasons to give the far [member lod_levels] entries cheaper meshes of their own, and to compare with [member cell_size] chunking before committing to this. [b]Note:[/b] This path has no LOD cross-fade. Overlapping [member FoliageLODLevel.visibility_range_begin]/[member FoliageLODLevel.visibility_range_end] bands are collapsed into contiguous ones so that every instance is drawn by exactly one level, and [member FoliageLODLevel.visibility_range_fade_mode] is ignored. [b]Note:[/b] Only the first four entries of [member lod_levels] are rendered, culling follows one camera: the viewport's current [Camera3D] at runtime, or the first 3D editor viewport in the editor (so other split views are culled against that one), and instances get no motion vectors (so they are not anti-aliased by TAA).

The path to a [MeshInstance3D] or [Landscape3D] that candidate points are projected onto when [member project_on_mesh] is enabled. For a [MeshInstance3D], only its mesh surface is used (its collision shape, if any, is ignored); for a [Landscape3D], its heightmap is sampled directly.

Read-only. The total number of instances across every cell created by the last [method regenerate] call. See [b]Cell chunking[/b] in the class description. While [member gpu_culling] is enabled this is how many instances were generated; how many of them survive culling is only ever known on the GPU.

The chain of [FoliageLODLevel]s (e.g. LOD_0, LOD_1, LOD_2) this spawner generates through, in order from highest to lowest detail. Every level shares the exact same generated instance transforms; only its mesh, material, and visibility/fade distance range differ (see [FoliageLODLevel]). A newly created [FoliageSpawner3D] starts with three levels with reasonable default distances, but this array can hold any number of levels, including just one (no LOD switching) or zero (nothing renders; see [method has_any_mesh]).
If [code]true[/code], inverts the values sampled from [member distribution_mask] (white areas become forbidden, black areas become favored).

A multiplier on the target instance count used to bound how many candidate points [method regenerate] will try before giving up. Increase this if strict [member min_distance] or [member distribution_mask] settings are preventing [member density] from being reached; decrease it to bound worst-case generation time.
A hard cap on the number of instances that can be generated, regardless of [member density] and the volume's size.
The upper bound of the random uniform scale applied to each instance. See also [member min_scale].
When [member project_on_mesh] is enabled, candidate points whose surface normal is tilted more than this many degrees from world up are discarded.
The minimum horizontal distance enforced between any two instances, measured on the volume's XZ footprint. Set to [code]0.0[/code] to disable spacing checks.
The lower bound of the random uniform scale applied to each instance. See also [member max_scale].

If [code]true[/code], each candidate point is projected onto the [MeshInstance3D] or [Landscape3D] referenced by [member ground_mesh_path], honoring [member max_slope_degrees]. For a [MeshInstance3D], this casts a ray straight down (in the volume's local space) from the top of [member volume_size] and snaps to the closest triangle hit, looking only at mesh geometry (no physics or collision shapes); points that hit nothing are discarded. For a [Landscape3D], the height field is sampled directly at the point's X/Z position instead (always hits, since a heightmap has no gaps). If [code]false[/code], points are instead placed at a random height inside the volume without any projection.
If [code]true[/code], each instance receives a random rotation around its up axis.
The maximum random tilt, in degrees, applied on top of [member align_to_normal] for natural-looking variation.
Pressing this button in the Inspector calls [method regenerate]. It is not meant to be read or assigned from code; use [method regenerate] directly instead.
The seed used to initialize the random number generator during [method regenerate]. Using the same seed with the same settings always produces the same result.
The size of the box volume that instances are scattered within, centered on the node's origin.
